caption: Fig. 1: While previous object recognition datasets have focused on (a) image classification, (b) object bounding box localization or (c) semantic pixel-level segmentation, we focus on (d) segmenting individual object instances. We introduce a large, richly-annotated dataset comprised of images depicting complex everyday scenes of common objects in their natural context.
description:

caption: Fig. 3: Our annotation pipeline is split into 3 primary tasks: (a) labeling the categories present in the image ( § 4.1), (b) locating and marking all instances of the labeled categories ( § 4.2), and (c) segmenting each object instance ( § 4.3).
description:

caption: Fig. 4: Worker precision and recall for the category labeling task. (a) The union of multiple AMT workers (blue) has better recall than any expert (red). Ground truth was computed using majority vote of the experts. (b) Shows the number of workers (circle size) and average number of jobs per worker (circle color) for each precision/recall range. Most workers have high precision; such workers generally also complete more jobs. For this plot ground truth for each worker is the union of responses from all other AMT workers. See § 4.4 for details.

caption: Fig. 5: (a) Number of annotated instances per category for MS COCO and PASCAL VOC. (b,c) Number of annotated categories and annotated instances, respectively, per image for MS COCO, ImageNet Detection, PASCAL VOC and SUN (average number of categories and instances are shown in parentheses). (d) Number of categories vs. the number of instances per category for a number of popular object recognition datasets. (e) The distribution of instance sizes for the MS COCO, ImageNet Detection, PASCAL VOC and SUN datasets.
description:
This figure is a collection of bar charts and line graphs comparing various object recognition datasets. Panel (a) shows the number of annotated instances per category for MS COCO and PASCAL VOC, with MS COCO having more instances across most categories. Panel (b) compares the number of categories per image across MS COCO, ImageNet Detection, PASCAL VOC, and SUN, with MS COCO having the highest average. Panel (c) shows the percentage of images with a certain number of instances, with MS COCO having the highest percentage of images with fewer instances. Panel (d) plots the number of categories against the number of instances per category, with Caltech Ped having the most instances per category. Panel (e) shows the distribution of instance sizes, with MS COCO having the highest percentage of small instances.

Text in figure: MS COCO, PASCAL VOC, ImageNet Detection, SUN, Caltech Ped, Caltech 256, Caltech 101, ImageNet Classification, Instances per category, Number of categories, Number of instances, Percent of instances, Percent of image size, 4%, 6%, 10%, 16%, 25%, 40%, 63%, 100%.

caption: Fig. 7: We visualize our mixture-specific shape masks. We paste thresholded shape masks on each candidate detection to generate candidate segments.
description:

This figure displays a series of grayscale images representing shape masks for different objects. Each row corresponds to a specific object category: Person, Bike, and Horse. Person
Bike
Horse

caption: Fig. 8: Evaluating instance detections with segmentation masks versus bounding boxes. Bounding boxes are a particularly crude approximation for articulated objects; in this case, the majority of the pixels in the ( blue ) tightfitting bounding-box do not lie on the object. Our ( green ) instance-level segmentation masks allows for a more accurate measure of object detection and localization.
description:
## Figure Description
This figure compares instance detections using segmentation masks and bounding boxes. The left panel shows a soccer player with a red flag and a soccer ball, illustrating the crudeness of bounding boxes for articulated objects. The right panel displays a green silhouette of the player, representing a more accurate instance-level segmentation mask.

## Text in Figure
- Bounding boxes
- Instance-level segmentation masks
- Blue tightfitting bounding-box
- Green instance-level segmentation mask
- More accurate measure of object detection and localization

caption: Fig. 9: A predicted segmentation might not recover object detail even though detection and ground truth bounding boxes overlap well (left). Sampling from the person category illustrates that predicting segmentations from topdown projection of DPM part masks is difficult even for correct detections (center). Average segmentation overlap measured on MS COCO for the 20 PASCAL VOC categories demonstrates the difficulty of the problem (right).
description:
## Description
This figure shows the challenges in predicting object segmentations. The left panel displays a predicted segmentation that does not recover object details despite good bounding box overlap. The center panel illustrates the difficulty of predicting segmentations from DPM part masks, even for correct detections. The right panel shows the average segmentation overlap for 20 PASCAL VOC categories, indicating the difficulty of the problem.

## Text in figure
Ground truth, Predicted, Category: person, DPM Segmentation Performance Baseline, Segmentatiation Overlap, Bounding Box Overlap, Average Overlap of Correct Detections, aeroplane, bicycle, bird, boat, bottle, bus, car, chair, cow, dog, diningtable, horse, motorbike, person, pottedplant, sheep, sofa, train, tvmonitor.

caption: Fig. 11: Icons of 91 categories in the MS COCO dataset grouped by 11 super-categories. We use these icons in our annotation pipeline to help workers quickly reference the indicated object category.
description:
## Figure Description
This figure is a visual representation of the 91 categories in the MS COCO dataset, organized into 11 super-categories. Each category is depicted by an icon, aiding annotators in quickly identifying the object category during the annotation process.

## Text in Figure
Icons of 91 categories in the MS COCO dataset grouped by 11 super-categories. Categories include: person & accessory, animal, vehicle, outdoor object, sports, kitchenware, food, furniture, appliance, electronics, indoor objects.

## Figure: Image annotation tasks

The figure shows three different image annotation tasks: category labeling, instance spotting, and instance segmentation. Each task is demonstrated with a sample image and instructions for the annotator.

## Index

### Tasks

- Category labeling
- Instance spotting
- Instance segmentation

### Instructions

- Select objects in the image
- Draw bounding boxes around objects
- Move target to the small object
- Please pay attention to trace boundary carefully
- Won't be rejected if not follow the instruction
